🫀 The Human Heart: A Beginner's Guide
Your heart is one of the most important organs in your body. It works 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, even when you're sleeping!
Think of your heart as a powerful pump that keeps blood moving throughout your body.
1. Where is your heart located?
File:Blausen 0458 Heart ThoracicCavity.png - Wikimedia Commons




Captured diagram






commons.wikimedia.org


Your heart is:
Located in your chest, between your lungs.



Slightly to the left of the center of your chest.



About the size of your fist.



Protected by your rib cage.




An adult heart typically weighs about 250–350 grams.
2. The four chambers of the heart
Your heart has four chambers, or rooms, that hold and move blood.
Heart Chambers Diagram — Free Printable Clipart for Teachers | Kuraplan




Captured diagram






kuraplan.com


Chamber
Job

Right atrium
Receives blood returning from the body

Right ventricle
Pumps blood to the lungs

Left atrium
Receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs

Left ventricle
Pumps blood to the entire body



Important: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it must pump blood throughout your body.
3. How does blood flow through the heart?
The heart works with your lungs to deliver oxygen to your organs.
Captured image

Simplified pathway of blood circulation
Here's what happens:
Blood low in oxygen returns from the body to the right side of the heart.



The right side pumps blood into the lungs.



The lungs add oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.



Oxygen-rich blood returns to the left side of the heart.



The left side pumps it to the rest of the body.




This cycle repeats continuously.
4. What makes your heart beat?
Your heart has its own electrical system!
A small group of specialized cells called the sinoatrial (SA) node acts as your heart's natural pacemaker.
It sends electrical signals that coordinate the heart's contractions.
10.5: Generation and Transmission of Cardiac Impulses - Medicine LibreTexts




Captured diagram






med.libretexts.org


A typical resting heart rate for an adult is 60–100 beats per minute. Well-trained athletes may have lower resting rates.
The familiar "lub-dub" sound comes mainly from your heart valves closing.
5. The four heart valves
Valves are like one-way doors. They prevent blood from flowing backward.
Valve

Between right atrium and right ventricle

Pulmonary
Between right ventricle and pulmonary artery

Mitral
Between left atrium and left ventricle

Aortic
Between left ventricle and aorta



6. How do you keep your heart healthy?

Exercise regularly
Walking, swimming, cycling, and running help strengthen your cardiovascular system.

Sleep supports healthy blood pressure and cardiovascular function.


Avoiding smoking, managing stress, and monitoring blood pressure also help protect your heart.

🫀 The Human Heart: A Beginner's Guide

Your heart is one of the most important organs in your body. It works 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, even when you're sleeping!

Think of your heart as a powerful pump that keeps blood moving throughout your body.

1. Where is your heart located?

commons.wikimedia.org

Your heart is:

  • Located in your chest, between your lungs.

  • Slightly to the left of the center of your chest.

  • About the size of your fist.

  • Protected by your rib cage.

An adult heart typically weighs about 250–350 grams.

2. The four chambers of the heart

Your heart has four chambers, or rooms, that hold and move blood.

kuraplan.com

Chamber

Job

Right atrium

Receives blood returning from the body

Right ventricle

Pumps blood to the lungs

Left atrium

Receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs

Left ventricle

Pumps blood to the entire body

Important: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it must pump blood throughout your body.

3. How does blood flow through the heart?

The heart works with your lungs to deliver oxygen to your organs.

Simplified pathway of blood circulation

Here's what happens:

  1. Blood low in oxygen returns from the body to the right side of the heart.

  2. The right side pumps blood into the lungs.

  3. The lungs add oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.

  4. Oxygen-rich blood returns to the left side of the heart.

  5. The left side pumps it to the rest of the body.

This cycle repeats continuously.

4. What makes your heart beat?

Your heart has its own electrical system!

A small group of specialized cells called the sinoatrial (SA) node acts as your heart's natural pacemaker.

It sends electrical signals that coordinate the heart's contractions.

med.libretexts.org

A typical resting heart rate for an adult is 60–100 beats per minute. Well-trained athletes may have lower resting rates.

The familiar "lub-dub" sound comes mainly from your heart valves closing.

5. The four heart valves

Valves are like one-way doors. They prevent blood from flowing backward.

Exercise regularly

Walking, swimming, cycling, and running help strengthen your cardiovascular system.

Choose vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and healthy fats while limiting excess salt.

Sleep supports healthy blood pressure and cardiovascular function.

turns.text: does all the valves open at the same time?
turns.html: does all the valves open at the same time?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text:
No! 🫀 The four heart valves do NOT open at the same time. They open and close in a coordinated sequence as your heart beats.
The valves work in two pairs.
1. When the ventricles relax (diastole)
OPEN
Tricuspid and mitral valves

 CLOSED 
Pulmonary and aortic valves

Blood flows from the atria into the ventricles.

2. When the ventricles contract (systole)
OPEN
Pulmonary and aortic valves

CLOSED
Tricuspid and mitral valves

Blood is pumped from the ventricles into the lungs and the rest of the body.

See how the valves work

Heart relaxesHeart contracts

Captured image

The ventricles fill with blood while the tricuspid and mitral valves are open.
Educational schematic, not an anatomical drawing. There are also brief moments when all four valves are closed.
Why don't all four open together?
Because blood needs to flow in one direction. If the inlet and outlet valves opened together at the wrong time, the heart couldn't build pressure and pump efficiently.
One more interesting fact: the valves don't open because the heart directly pulls them open. They open and close because of pressure differences on either side of each valve.
Quick question: When the left ventricle contracts to pump blood into the aorta, should the mitral valve be open or closed?

turns.html: does purify the blood?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text:
The heart does not purify or clean the blood directly. 🫀 Its main job is to pump blood to organs that perform different functions.
Three important organs are involved:
🫀 Heart: Pumps blood throughout the body.



🫁 Lungs: Remove carbon dioxide from the blood and add oxygen.



Kidneys: Filter waste products and excess water from the blood, producing urine.




The liver also helps process toxins, medications, and waste substances.
How does it work?
Body → Heart
Blood returns with less oxygen and more carbon dioxide

Captured diagram

Lungs
Carbon dioxide is removed and oxygen is added

Captured diagram

Heart → Body
Oxygen-rich blood is pumped throughout the body


Meanwhile, the kidneys continuously filter blood, removing waste and helping maintain the right balance of water and salts.
Remember: The heart is the pump, the lungs are responsible for gas exchange, and the kidneys are the body's main blood filters.
Would you like to learn why blood goes to the lungs before returning to the heart, instead of going directly to the body?
